clue.text: Disorganised guy in untidy dwelling

indicators.note: in tells us the fellow's word is placed inside the word for the dwelling

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, the byword for a messy home
cat is old slang for a man or fellow, as in a cool cat

explanation.surface: A muddled man living in a messy house.
explanation.definitionFit: Scatty is informal British for absent-minded and muddled, so it is a synonym of disorganised.

clue.text: Unruly lot led by guerrilla's voice

indicators.note: led by puts the guerrilla's word in front of the jumbled letters

parts.note: the Contras were the rebel guerrillas of Nicaragua in the 1980s

indicators.note: unruly suggests the letters of the word lot are out of order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A disorderly band of fighters following a rebel's call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' reorders the three letters of 'lot'; 'led by' puts the rebel word first.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is the lowest female singing voice, so it is an example of a voice.

clue.text: Before drink runs short, samples port

indicators.note: before places the word for samples ahead of the shortened drink

parts.note: to sample something is to try it, so samples gives tries

indicators.note: runs short says the word for the drink loses its final letter

parts.note: tea is the everyday British drink

explanation.surface: Someone tasting things in a harbour bar before the drink runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs short' cuts TEA to TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a major seaport on the Adriatic in north-east Italy, so it is an example of a port.

clue.text: Vegetable needing a month to come up

indicators.note: in a down clue, to come up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: May is one month of the year

explanation.surface: A crop that needs a month before it sprouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come up' turns MAY round to YAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A yam is a starchy tropical tuber eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Objective, being sent on special assignment

definitions.meaning: objective means impartial, standing apart from personal feeling
an officer seconded to a special unit is said to be on this kind of posting

explanation.surface: An impartial person sent off on a special mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Detached means both aloof and impartial, and in military usage posted away from one's unit on special duty.

clue.text: Pupil expected to absorb only first bits of National Curriculum?

indicators.note: to absorb means the word for expected takes the picked letters inside it

parts.note: something due is expected, as a train due at noon

indicators.note: first bits of means take the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A schoolchild expected to take in only the basics of the national syllabus.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Curriculum is the set syllabus for schools in England; 'to absorb' puts its initials inside the word for expected.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow pupil, the classroom duffer, so the definition is a particular kind of pupil.

clue.text: Follow betting odds about start of the races

parts.note: to track someone is to follow them

indicators.note: about means the betting word goes round the picked letter

parts.note: evens is the betting price at which the stake is doubled

indicators.note: start of means take only the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A punter following the odds at the beginning of race day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes T from 'the', and 'about' puts EVENS round it, giving EVENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Track events are the running races in athletics, so they are races.

clue.text: Old nut cake

definitions.meaning: old slang for the head, as in being off one's rocker
a soft spongy griddle cake toasted and eaten with butter

explanation.surface: An elderly nutty person offered a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: A crumpet is a British teacake, a spongy griddle cake toasted for tea; 'off one's crumpet' is old slang meaning out of one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumpet is dated British slang for the head and also the name of a toasted griddle cake.

clue.text: Essayist's written about unknown girl

indicators.note: written about says the essayist's name is set around the unknown

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of Charles Lamb, author of the Essays of Elia
z is a standard algebraic unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A writer's piece about a mysterious young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' puts ELIA round Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliza is a girl's name, a short form of Elizabeth.

clue.text: Ships wrecked in mined area are nowhere to be seen

indicators.note: wrecked suggests the remaining letters are broken up and reassembled
nowhere to be seen says the word are vanishes from the phrase in front of it

parts.note: the word are itself is removed from the letters

explanation.surface: Vessels sunk in a mined sea area have disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nowhere to be seen' strips ARE from INMINEDAREA, leaving INMINEDA, which 'wrecked' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: East Indiamen were large merchant ships trading with India, so the word names a class of ship.

clue.text: Drivers coming across sheepdog in part of Italy

indicators.note: coming across says the drivers' letters straddle the dog's name

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British motoring organisation
the puli is a Hungarian sheepdog with a corded coat

explanation.surface: Motorists encounter a sheepdog on an Italian road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming across' wraps the motoring body's letters round the Hungarian dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Apulia is the region forming the heel of Italy, now usually called Puglia.

clue.text: Verification of language spoken after indication of error

indicators.note: after places the sounded language behind the error mark

parts.note: a teacher marks a wrong answer with a cross

indicators.note: spoken says the language name is said aloud and spelt as its sound-alike

parts.note: Czech is the language of the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: Checking a speech in a foreign tongue after a mistake is marked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken' turns CZECH into CHECK, its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-check confirms a fact by using a second source, so it is a means of verification.

clue.text: Main theme of Friends broadcast in oral America, dear

indicators.note: broadcast in oral suggests words spoken on air and scattered, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Talking to a dear American friend about the TV show's central idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast in oral' rearranges AMERICA plus DEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Camaraderie is friendly fellowship among companions, the central theme of the sitcom Friends.

clue.text: Drama in royal palace after revolution

indicators.note: after revolution says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A theatrical performance staged in a royal residence after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The run YALP sits across 'royal palace'; 'after revolution' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a piece of drama written for the stage.

clue.text: Escape viral illness, taking vitamin

parts.note: flu, influenza, is a viral illness
vitamin E is one of the lettered vitamins

explanation.surface: Avoiding a virus by taking a vitamin supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Escape' is a noun here: an outlet for smoke or gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A flue is a duct or chimney through which smoke and gases escape.

clue.text: They drive cars without current tax displayed

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cars word goes round the rest

parts.note: motors is informal for cars
I is the symbol for electric current
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: Cars on show without the road tax disc being displayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Motivators are people or things that drive others on, so they are what drives.

clue.text: Boat train missing terminus

indicators.note: missing terminus says the train's word loses its end letter

parts.note: the Tube is the London Underground railway, so a tube is a train

explanation.surface: A boat train that does not reach its terminal station.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's underground railway; 'missing terminus' drops its last letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Tub is informal for a slow, clumsy boat.

clue.text: Handing back capital, perhaps soldiers find gun in a heap

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: in a heap suggests the letters are piled up in disorder and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Troops discover a weapon lying in a pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a heap' jumbles 'find gun'; capital is money, as in a business's funds.
explanation.definitionFit: Refunding means paying money back, and capital is one example of what may be repaid, hence the perhaps.

clue.text: Plump Christmas bird, note

parts.note: round means plump, chubby
the robin is the bird pictured on British Christmas cards

explanation.surface: A fat robin on a Christmas card.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is a letter or note sent to many people, such as a Christmas newsletter.

clue.text: Worthy of attention, as 5 dn is?

definitions.meaning: the slow pupil of 5 down read as two words: lacking ability

explanation.surface: Is a dunce worth noticing?
explanation.walkthrough: 5 down is DUNCE, who is NOT ABLE, read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable means remarkable, deserving notice.

clue.text: Half portion of sweet, posh nosh for vegetarians

indicators.note: half portion of says only the first three of six letters of the sweet are kept

parts.note: toffee is a chewy sweet
U means upper-class, from the U and non-U classification

explanation.surface: Half a helping of pudding and some smart food for vegetarians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half portion of' keeps TOF from TOFFEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is bean curd, a protein food much eaten by vegetarians; nosh is slang for food.

clue.text: Small monkey died dropping out of tree

indicators.note: dropping out of says the letter for died falls away from the tree word

parts.note: the tamarind is a tropical tree with edible pods

explanation.surface: A dead creature falls from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping out of' removes D from TAMARIND.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamarin is a small South American monkey related to the marmosets.

clue.text: Stay on western island

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river, especially the Thames

explanation.surface: Remaining on an island in the west.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait is to stay where one is.

clue.text: Trouble with sailors below deck

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble, as in much ado
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Seamen causing a fuss down in the hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' puts RN under ADO in this down entry; 'deck' is a verb, to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to decorate, as in deck the halls, so it is a synonym of adorn.

clue.text: Rich man's anguish, losing gold in business sell-off

parts.note: Dives is the traditional name of the rich man in the parable of Lazarus

indicators.note: losing says the gold letters are taken out of the anguish word

parts.note: torment means anguish
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A wealthy tycoon suffers when stripped of assets in a company sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes OR from TORMENT, leaving TMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Divestment is the sale of a business or its assets, so it is a business sell-off.

clue.text: Evil at core of French love film

indicators.note: at core means take only the central letters of the word

parts.note: de is French for of
o is zero, love in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A wicked French romance on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at core' takes VI from EVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A video is a recorded film.

clue.text: Medic carried in South African aircraft

indicators.note: carried in says the medic's letters are held inside the South African's

parts.note: a Boer is a South African of Dutch descent
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor flown in a South African plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried in' places the doctor's degree inside the Afrikaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomber is a military aircraft that drops bombs.

clue.text: Being 1 is characteristic associated with daughter

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic

explanation.surface: A girl inheriting a family trait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being 1' points to 1 across: the definition reads as being disorganised and muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Distrait means absent-minded and distracted, which matches the muddled state of 1 across.

clue.text: We're told several pupils find it a problem

indicators.note: we're told means the word is heard rather than read, a sound-alike

parts.note: some means several, an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Several schoolchildren report finding something difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We're told' turns SOME into SUM, its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum is an arithmetic problem set to schoolchildren.

clue.text: Only cricket side to be backed by an American

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to be backed says the two words that come first are read backwards together

parts.note: one means only, as in the one person
leg, or the on side, is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A lone cricket team supported by one American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be backed' reverses ONELEG to GELENO, which follows AN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Angeleno is a native or resident of Los Angeles, so an American.

clue.text: Household in which people get on

parts.note: men means people
to age is to get on in years

explanation.surface: A home where everyone gets along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get on' looks like getting along; it means growing older.
explanation.definitionFit: A menage is a household, from the French word for housekeeping.
